## Finding: No — SMOTE does not change >50K F1 by more than 0.02

**Primary metric: ΔF1 (SMOTE − none) = −0.0026**, mean over 25 paired CV folds. That's about an eighth of the 0.02 threshold, and in the *negative* direction.

| | F1 (>50K) | Precision | Recall | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No resampling | 0.6601 | 0.7046 | 0.6210 | 0.8913 |
| SMOTE | 0.6574 | 0.6819 | 0.6348 | 0.8868 |

SMOTE does exactly what you'd expect mechanically — it buys **+1.4 pts of recall for −2.3 pts of precision** — but on this dataset those two effects nearly cancel in F1, and ranking quality (AUC) is slightly *worse*. There is no free lunch here; SMOTE is acting mostly as an implicit threshold shift, and F1 at a fixed 0.5 threshold is close to indifferent to it.

**Stability checks — all four held up:**
- **5×5 repeated stratified CV** (25 paired folds): Δ = −0.0026, 95% bootstrap CI **[−0.0038, −0.0015]**. The CI excludes both +0.02 and −0.02. **0 of 25** individual folds exceeded |Δ| = 0.02.
- **Statistically detectable but practically negligible**: paired t = −4.45, p = 0.00017. With 25 paired folds the tiny decrease is real — it's just an order of magnitude too small to matter.
- **10 different RF/SMOTE seeds** on a fixed split: Δ ranged [−0.0072, +0.0003].
- **Fresh re-test split** (unused in the initial analysis): Δ = −0.0006.
- **SMOTENC sensitivity** (plain SMOTE interpolates one-hot columns into fractional values, which is methodologically dubious): Δ = +0.0056. The *sign flips*, but the magnitude stays ~4× below 0.02 — so the conclusion survives, though the sign of the residual is encoding-dependent and shouldn't be over-read.

**Key methodological choice worth flagging:** SMOTE is applied *inside* an imblearn pipeline, so it only ever fits on training folds. Resampling before the split is a common error that leaks synthetic neighbours of test points into training and would inflate the apparent benefit substantially. Also note the metric is fixed at the default 0.5 threshold — with threshold tuning on either arm, most of SMOTE's apparent effect disappears entirely.

Files written: `result.json`, `analysis.py`, plus `cv_fold_results.csv` with the per-fold numbers.

One housekeeping note unrelated to the analysis: the Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Drive connectors are unauthorized in this session and can't be authorized from a non-interactive run — you'd need to connect them in your claude.ai connector settings if you want them available.

parsed_result.summary: No. With a default RandomForestClassifier, SMOTE oversampling changes the >50K F1 score by only -0.0026 (95% bootstrap CI [-0.0038, -0.0015]) across 25 paired CV folds -- far short of the 0.02 threshold, and the CI excludes both +0.02 and -0.02. The small shift that does occur is a trade of precision (0.705 -> 0.682) for recall (0.621 -> 0.635), with ranking quality (ROC-AUC 0.8913 -> 0.8868) essentially unchanged.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Minority-class (>50K) F1 difference (SMOTE - no resampling), mean over 5x5 repeated stratified CV
parsed_result.direction: No meaningful change (|delta F1| = 0.0026 < 0.02); SMOTE trades precision for recall at near-identical F1
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Features: all columns except fnlwgt (census sampling weight, not a person-level attribute); education kept alongside education-num. Missing values ('?' read as NaN) imputed as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped; the 52 exact duplicate rows were kept. Categoricals one-hot encoded (handle_unknown='ignore'), numerics passed through unscaled since trees are scale-invariant. Classifier fixed at RandomForestClassifier() defaults (100 trees, no depth limit, no class_weight); only random_state was set, for reproducibility. SMOTE used imblearn defaults (k_neighbors=5, full 1:1 balancing) and was applied inside an imblearn Pipeline so it fits on training folds only -- resampling before splitting would leak synthetic neighbours into the test set and inflate the effect. Metric: F1 of the >50K class at the default 0.5 threshold (no threshold tuning; threshold tuning would change the answer, as most of SMOTE's effect here is an implicit threshold shift). Primary estimate is the paired within-fold difference over 5x5 repeated stratified CV on all 48842 rows; a single stratified 80/20 holdout was run first as the initial analysis. Plain SMOTE interpolates one-hot columns into fractional values, so SMOTENC was run as a sensitivity check.
parsed_result.verification_method: Four checks. (1) 5x5 repeated stratified 5-fold CV (25 paired folds, repeat seeds 0-4), paired t-test plus a 10000-draw percentile bootstrap CI over fold-level differences. (2) Seed sensitivity: 10 different RF/SMOTE random_state values on the fixed seed-42 holdout. (3) A fresh held-out 80/20 re-test split (seed 20260831) not used in the initial analysis. (4) SMOTENC instead of plain SMOTE over 5 folds.
parsed_result.verification_result: Held up on all four. Initial 80/20 holdout gave delta F1 = -0.0038. Repeated CV: F1 none 0.6601 vs SMOTE 0.6574, mean delta -0.0026 (sd 0.0030), 95% bootstrap CI [-0.0038, -0.0015], paired t = -4.45, p = 0.000168; 0/25 individual folds exceeded |delta| = 0.02. Across 10 model seeds on the holdout, delta ranged [-0.0072, +0.0003]. Fresh re-test split: delta = -0.0006. SMOTENC gave mean delta +0.0056 over 5 folds -- the sign flips versus plain SMOTE, but the magnitude stays roughly 4x below 0.02, so the no-meaningful-change conclusion is not an artifact of interpolating one-hot columns (only the sign of the tiny residual is). The plain-SMOTE decrease is statistically detectable (p < 0.001) but an order of magnitude below the 0.02 practical threshold.
